# /handoff

The ledger is **what is true**. The board is what is next. Keep them apart: a fact in the board
rots the moment its item is done.

## Reading it

Read it first, every session, in full, before the board and before any code; of the files in `passoff/`, read only your own item's. Its Settled sections are
closed: **do not re-ask anything recorded there.** Its claims are leads, not facts: re-verify
before building on one, and record your verification with its own date and citation in place of
the original's.

## Recording work

**A closed item's record is the close-out section at the end of its own file**,
`passoff/<n>-<slug>.md`, written by the session that did the work. It names what changed, why, what is now fixed, which questions it answered,
and what is left owed. The file is its writer's own: never edit another item's close-out.

**Then one line at the end of `## Log`**: `- <date> · closed item <n>`. Cite the item by its
number, never its path: the file moves to the archive at the next fold, and the number still
finds it. Work that is not an item, such as an `/autopilot` run or a fix the owner asked for in
chat, gets one line that ends in the path of what it wrote.

`personal-config handoff step` prints both scaffolds and writes nothing. Where this ledger once
had numbered steps, they are in the archive's `HANDOFF-log.md`, and a
`DONE - HANDOFF <n>` row still points at one of them.

**On a 1.x board, with no `passoff/` folder beside it**, the record is one step in this ledger at the next free number,
read from the file, and a step you did not write is never edited.

## Editing a standing section

Environment, Settled, Code map, Invariants, Known facts are edited in place when they go stale,
never appended to. Two rules hold everywhere in this file:

- **Absolute dates only.** `2026-09-15`, never "today" or "recently". This is read months later
  by an agent with no idea when it was written.
- **Every claim carries a citation**: `file:line`, a commit, a migration name, or the command
  that produced it. A claim with no citation is a guess and will be treated as one.

**Run every gate command once before writing it into Environment.** A command in a doc that has
never been run in this repo is a trap for every session after you.

**Decisions, Zach's, asked in one batch before code (2026-10-26). He took every recommended option.**
(1) Any slot that overlaps the window is away (the issue's criterion 1). The fully-inside rule would show
slots that `ensureAvailableUsers` then rejects. (2) The panel keeps today's text; its place between the slots
shows the window. No new string, no attendee-zone times, and that answers the host-zone question: placement is
enough. (3) Two windows on one day give two panels, one per run of away slots. (4) Criterion 4, the "Book
<name>" redirect, stays, shown by a unit test and a hand-edited `toUserId` row in the walk.

**Shipped (5 code files, 5 test files).**
- `date-ranges.ts`: `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows(entries, timeZone)` returns, per partial entry, the
  `wallClockToTimeZone` instants and every host-zone date the window touches (stepped in UTC so DST cannot move
  a boundary). `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` now delegates to it. `buildDateRanges` skips away-map dates
  that carry `windows` when it removes whole days from `oooExcludedDateRanges`.
- `getUserAvailability.ts`: `IOutOfOfficeData[date]` gains optional `windows: IOutOfOfficeWindow[]` (ISO
  `start`/`end` plus the entry data); a date with windows carries the first window's data at the top level
  so old readers still work. `toOutOfOfficeEntryData` is the one place that maps an entry to that shape (the
  whole-day reducer used to do it inline). `calculateOutOfOfficeRanges` takes the windows as a third
  argument; a whole-day record wins over a window on the same date, and a holiday replaces windows but not a
  whole-day record. Partial windows stay in `dateRanges` and are subtracted only from
  `oooExcludedDateRanges` (with the busy times), the same split whole days have.
- `slots.ts`: `parseOutOfOfficeWindows` turns the windows into epoch-ms once per `getSlots` call;
  `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` marks a slot away for a windowed date only if `slotStart < end && slotEnd > start`.
  Whole-day marking is untouched.
- `AvailableTimes.tsx`: one loop renders a `SlotItem` per bookable slot and one `OOOSlot` at the first slot
  of each away run (`pb-0` when the run ends the list). The all-away branch is unchanged.
- `AvailableTimeSlots.tsx`: `isOOODay` is `every(away)` instead of the first slot, so a window that starts
  the day no longer hides the time-format toggle.
- Not changed, checked: `DatePicker.tsx` (`every(away)` already), `useNonEmptyScheduleDays.ts` and the weekly
  `Empty.tsx` (both need every slot away to treat a day as away), API v2 `slots-output.service.ts` (filters
  `away`), team events (`getAggregatedAvailability` uses `oooExcludedDateRanges`, out of scope).

    bootstrap(app);
    await generateSwaggerForApp(app);

  }

```text
import { getEnv } from "@/env";
import { Logger } from "@nestjs/common";
import type { NestExpressApplication } from "@nestjs/platform-express";
import { SwaggerModule, DocumentBuilder } from "@nestjs/swagger";
import type {
  PathItemObject,
  PathsObject,
  OperationObject,
} from "@nestjs/swagger/dist/interfaces/open-api-spec.interface";
import "dotenv/config";
import * as fs from "node:fs";
import type { Server } from "node:http";
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { createRequire } from "node:module";

const nodeRequire = createRequire(__filename);
const biomeBin = nodeRequire.resolve("@biomejs/biome/bin/biome");

const HttpMethods: (keyof PathItemObject)[] = ["get", "post", "put", "delete", "patch", "options", "head"];

export async function generateSwaggerForApp(app: NestExpressApplication<Server>) {
  const logger = new Logger("App");
  logger.log(`Generating Swagger documentation...\n`);

  const config = new DocumentBuilder().setTitle("Cal.diy API v2").build();
  const document = SwaggerModule.createDocument(app, config);
  document.paths = groupAndSortPathsByFirstTag(document.paths);

  const docsOutputFile = "../../../docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json";
  const stringifiedContents = JSON.stringify(document, null, 2);

  if (fs.existsSync(docsOutputFile) && getEnv("NODE_ENV") === "development") {
    fs.unlinkSync(docsOutputFile);
    fs.writeFileSync(docsOutputFile, stringifiedContents, { encoding: "utf8" });
    spawnSync("node", [biomeBin, "format", "--write", docsOutputFile], { stdio: "inherit" });
  }

  if (!process.env.DOCS_URL) {
    SwaggerModule.setup("docs", app, document, {
      customCss: ".swagger-ui .topbar { display: none }",
    });

    logger.log(`Swagger documentation available in the "/docs" endpoint\n`);
  }
}

function groupAndSortPathsByFirstTag(paths: PathsObject): PathsObject {
  const groupedPaths: { [key: string]: PathsObject } = {};

  Object.keys(paths).forEach((pathKey) => {
    const pathItem = paths[pathKey];

    HttpMethods.forEach((method) => {
      const operation = pathItem[method];

      if (isOperationObject(operation) && operation.tags && operation.tags.length > 0) {
        const firstTag = operation.tags[0];

        if (!groupedPaths[firstTag]) {
          groupedPaths[firstTag] = {};
        }

        groupedPaths[firstTag][pathKey] = pathItem;
      }
    });
  });

  const sortedTags = Object.keys(groupedPaths).sort(customTagSort);
  const sortedPaths: PathsObject = {};

  sortedTags.forEach((tag) => {
    Object.assign(sortedPaths, groupedPaths[tag]);
  });

  return sortedPaths;
}

function customTagSort(a: string, b: string): number {
  const platformPrefix = "Platform";
  const orgsPrefix = "Orgs";

  if (a.startsWith(platformPrefix) && !b.startsWith(platformPrefix)) {
    return -1;
  }
  if (!a.startsWith(platformPrefix) && b.startsWith(platformPrefix)) {
    return 1;
  }

  if (a.startsWith(orgsPrefix) && !b.startsWith(orgsPrefix)) {
    return -1;
  }
  if (!a.startsWith(orgsPrefix) && b.startsWith(orgsPrefix)) {
    return 1;
  }

  return a.localeCompare(b);
}

function isOperationObject(obj: any): obj is OperationObject {
  return obj && typeof obj === "object" && "tags" in obj;
}

import type { CreateEventTypeInput_2024_06_14 } from "@calcom/platform-types";
import { BadRequestException } from "@nestjs/common";

import { InputEventTypesService_2024_06_14 } from "./input-event-types.service";

import type { EventTypesRepository_2024_06_14 } from "@/platform/event-types/event-types_2024_06_14/event-types.repository";

type ColorInput = CreateEventTypeInput_2024_06_14["color"];

describe("InputEventTypesService_2024_06_14", () => {
  let service: InputEventTypesService_2024_06_14;

  beforeEach(() => {
    service = new InputEventTypesService_2024_06_14(
      {} as EventTypesRepository_2024_06_14,
      {} as CalendarsService
    );
  });

  describe("validateInputBookingPageColors", () => {
    const accentColors = { lightThemeHex: "#292929", darkThemeHex: "#fafafa" };

    it("accepts a request without color", () => {
      expect(() => service.validateInputBookingPageColors(undefined)).not.toThrow();
    });

    it("accepts accent colors without booking page colors", () => {
      expect(() => service.validateInputBookingPageColors(accentColors)).not.toThrow();
    });

    it("accepts six and three digit hex booking page colors", () => {
      const color: ColorInput = {
        ...accentColors,
        bookingPageBackgroundHex: "#1e293b",
        bookingPageTextHex: "#FFF",
      };

      expect(() => service.validateInputBookingPageColors(color)).not.toThrow();
    });

    it("accepts null, which clears a stored booking page color", () => {
      const color: ColorInput = {
        ...accentColors,
        bookingPageBackgroundHex: null,
        bookingPageTextHex: null,
      };

      expect(() => service.validateInputBookingPageColors(color)).not.toThrow();
    });

    it("rejects a background color that is not hex", () => {
      const color: ColorInput = { ...accentColors, bookingPageBackgroundHex: "red" };

      expect(() => service.validateInputBookingPageColors(color)).toThrow(
        new BadRequestException("color.bookingPageBackgroundHex must be a hex color such as #ffffff")
      );
    });

    // @IsHexColor accepts a value without "#", but the stored eventTypeColor schema does not.
    it("rejects a text color without the leading #", () => {
      const color: ColorInput = { ...accentColors, bookingPageTextHex: "ffffff" };

      expect(() => service.validateInputBookingPageColors(color)).toThrow(
        new BadRequestException("color.bookingPageTextHex must be a hex color such as #ffffff")
      );
    });

    it("rejects a hex value of the wrong length", () => {
      const color: ColorInput = { ...accentColors, bookingPageTextHex: "#ffff" };

      expect(() => service.validateInputBookingPageColors(color)).toThrow(BadRequestException);
    });

    it("rejects a value that is not a string", () => {
      const color = { ...accentColors, bookingPageBackgroundHex: 123 } as unknown as ColorInput;

      expect(() => service.validateInputBookingPageColors(color)).toThrow(
        new BadRequestException("color.bookingPageBackgroundHex must be a hex color such as #ffffff")
      );
    });
  });
});

import * as fs from "fs-extra";
import * as path from "node:path";

// First, copyNestSwagger is required to enable "@nestjs/swagger" in the "nest-cli.json",
// because nest-cli.json is resolving "@nestjs/swagger" plugin from
// project's node_modules, but due to dependency hoisting, the "@nestjs/swagger" is located in the root node_modules.
// Second, we need to run this before starting the application using "nest start", because "nest start" is ran by
// "nest-cli" with the "nest-cli.json" file, and for nest cli to be loaded with plugins correctly the "@nestjs/swagger"
// should reside in the project's node_modules already before the "nest start" command is executed.
async function copyNestSwagger() {
  const monorepoRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, "../../../../../");
  const nodeModulesNestjs = path.resolve(__dirname, "../../node_modules/@nestjs");
  const swaggerModulePath = "@nestjs/swagger";

  const sourceDir = path.join(monorepoRoot, "node_modules", swaggerModulePath);
  const targetDir = path.join(nodeModulesNestjs, "swagger");

  if (!(await fs.pathExists(targetDir))) {
    try {
      await fs.ensureDir(nodeModulesNestjs);
      await fs.copy(sourceDir, targetDir);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error("Failed to copy @nestjs/swagger:", error);
    }
  }
}

copyNestSwagger();
```
